source.description: arq_uuid accepted from caller (KB entry-point) and interpolated into Cyborg API URL path in get_arq_by_uuid

sink.description: HTTP GET /accelerator_requests/{arq_uuid}: arq_uuid concatenated into URL path via "/".join([self.ARQ_URL, arq_uuid]) without UUID-format or path-character validation

stoppedAt.detail: get_arq_by_uuid (defined at cyborg.py:337) does not appear anywhere in the 443-file source set — grep over src/ confirms it is only the definition. Five files call into cyborg.py (compute/api.py, compute/manager.py, compute/utils.py, conductor/manager.py, network/neutron.py) but all call get_client, get_device_profile_request_groups, get_arq_pci_device_profile, or get_device_amount_of_dp_groups. The callers of get_arq_by_uuid are in files not yet extracted from the nova codebase. New namespaces added in this pass (nova.hacking, nova.image, nova.keymgr, nova.limit) contain no callers.

sanitisationGaps: No UUID format check or path-character filtering visible between method parameter (line 337) and HTTP call (lines 358-359) in get_arq_by_uuid.

evaluatedFindings.title: SHA-224 used in generate_hostid

evaluatedFindings.title: User-controlled scheduler hint used as getattr attribute on HostState
evaluatedFindings.reason: Confidence is needs_cross_file. KB securitySurface is empty. Scheduler filters are loaded by dynamic dispatch from config — no inbound static edges even with 443 files in source set.

evaluatedFindings.title: HMAC validation of metadata proxy request conditionally skipped when shared secret is unconfigured
evaluatedFindings.reason: Finding (276-280) does not overlap the only KB entry-point (line 97). CWE-306 auth-bypass is a standalone information-disclosure vulnerability, not a taint-injection chain.

evaluatedFindings.title: TLS hostname verification disabled in VeNCrypt security handshake
evaluatedFindings.reason: KB securitySurface is empty — no entry-point entries. The finding describes a TLS configuration weakness (CWE-297) on the outbound connection to QEMU VNC backend; it is not an injection taint source. An attacker would need a CA-signed certificate for a different compute node and network access to the management network to exploit this.
